topics.topic: AuditEntry identity, storage, and identifier minting
questions: What makes two otherwise equal AuditEntry entities distinct, and does Registry mint an audit-entry identifier?
What identifies one AuditEntry, who creates that identity, and is it a stored model fact?
What gives each AuditEntry its distinct identity?

quotes: Substitution: two entries with equal facts are two events — two archivings of two projects at the same instant, or an erasure and its re-run — and the log is read in time order as distinct entries (R0-58).
judgement.divergence: One implementer gives every AuditEntry a Registry-minted stored identifier and preserves equal entries under distinct identities; another treats event occurrence or storage position as sufficient and stores no identifier, which the owner notices if audit entries expose or require a stable individual reference.
judgement.why: State 1 declares AuditEntry an entity but does not identify the fact that constitutes its identity or say who creates it.

topics.topic: Subject representation for AuditEntries not tied to a Project or Customer
questions: What subject fact does an AuditEntry carry when the action changes no Project or Customer?
What subject fact does each non-project/non-customer AuditEntry carry, especially a declined access-request answer and erasure of old audit entries?
What subject fact does each import entry and old-audit-erasure entry carry, and may an AuditEntry have no project, customer or session subject?

quotes:
the change: which action, in a closed vocabulary State 6 declares. The
  actions that write an entry (R0-58): creating, correcting, archiving,
  anonymising and deleting a project; recording, correcting and erasing a
  customer; restricting and lifting; ending and resuming a relationship;
  granting a project to a session, revoking one and answering a request; the
  import, as one entry whose subject is the migration closure (M10); erasing
  old entries.
for an erasure of old entries: the date the owner gave (R0-66).
judgement.divergence: One implementer permits an AuditEntry with no project, customer or session subject for a decline or audit-log erasure; another assigns a synthetic log, session, or migration subject, and the owner notices the different subjects in the audit view.
judgement.why: The text requires these entries but does not define their subject facts consistently.

topics.topic: Whether Room stores the ActingPrincipal that added it
questions: Does a Room carry the ActingPrincipal that added it?
Does a Room carry the ActingPrincipal that added it?
Does a Room store the acting principal that added it, or not?

quotes:
Who added it — the owner or the agent through Kernel — is not a fact of the
room: no stated requirement reads it, State 0's output of "add a room" names
id, name and project only, and a session identity would otherwise reach every
reader of the rooms (round 1 T11).

Who did something, as Registry records it in an audit entry (R0-37), on a room
and on a pointer (M03, M05): the owner, signed in with the owner credential
(R0-30); a service, named by its service token (R0-27); or the agent through
Cabinet Kernel, naming the session Kernel named (R0-53).
Embedded in audit entries, rooms and pointers.
judgement.why: M03 expressly excludes the adding principal from Room while M07 expressly embeds ActingPrincipal in rooms.

topics.topic: Whether answering or declining an access request creates an AuditEntry
questions: Does declining an access request create an AuditEntry?
Does declining an access request, or answering one independently of the resulting grant, create an AuditEntry?
Does every answer to an access request create an audit entry, including a decline that only clears the request, or is only an answer that grants a project audited as a grant?

quotes:
Registry records only significant changes of state: changes to projects and
customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects,
restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations.

the change: which action, in a closed vocabulary State 6 declares. The
  actions that write an entry (R0-58): creating, correcting, archiving,
  anonymising and deleting a project; recording, correcting and erasing a
  customer; restricting and lifting; ending and resuming a relationship;
  granting a project to a session, revoking one and answering a request; the
  import, as one entry whose subject is the migration closure (M10); erasing
  old entries.
judgement.why: State 0 limits audit entries to its listed state changes, while M09 additionally says answering a request writes an entry, including an answer that may only clear the request.

topics.topic: Authoritative allocation of model facts, optionality, timestamps, and creation inputs between states
questions: Which models must carry created and last-changed instants, and do the model-specific fact lists override the general statement?
Must State 1 completely settle each model’s facts, their optionality and the facts supplied at creation, or may State 6 add or remove facts and decide optionality?

quotes:
A
record carries the instant it was created and the instant it was last
changed; `registry_updated_at` in `context` is the project's last-changed
instant (R0-04, L16).

A room and a pointer have no last-changed instant:
  they are written once (a pointer's status change records its own instant).
judgement.why: The general rule gives every record a last-changed instant, while the specific rule denies that fact to Room and ArtifactPointer.

topics.topic: Provenance and withdrawal facts assigned to imported legacy ArtifactPointers when absent from the source
questions: What publication and withdrawal principals and withdrawal instant does an imported legacy pointer carry when the source did not record them?
What published-by principal, withdrawn instant and withdrawn-by principal does an imported pointer carry when the VPS source does not hold those facts?

quotes:
written once: the instant it was published and by which principal (M07) —
  a producer service as its token names it, Kernel for the agent naming its
  session, or the owner for any owner service; the instant it was superseded;
  the instant it was withdrawn and by which principal (R0-14).

A record the import brings in keeps the instants its source holds: a
project's created, last-changed and archived instants, a room's added
instant, a pointer's published and superseded instants.

the import keeps every v1
project, room and pointer id verbatim (R0-44, R0-50, R0-79).
judgement.divergence: One implementer rejects a legacy pointer lacking the mandatory publication or withdrawal provenance; another imports it with absent or synthetic provenance, which the owner notices through import success and the resulting pointer history.
judgement.why: The model requires provenance facts for every pointer but defines no value or absence rule when the imported source lacks them.

topics.topic: Whether confirmed no-op or refused actions mint confirmation ids and create AuditEntries
questions: Does an accepted action that makes no state change—such as archiving an already archived project, anonymising an already anonymised project, or erasing an already erased customer—create an AuditEntry and confirmation id?
Is a confirmation id minted and an audit entry written when a confirmed action is a no-op or is refused?

quotes:
the outcome (accepted; whether refused attempts are recorded is settled in
  State 2, round 28 P1);

Which actions must state
the revision they were made against is State 2's (carried, R0-35).
judgement.why: Whether a confirmed invocation is accepted, refused, treated as a no-op, and consequently emits an audit entry or confirmation id is an operation rule owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Whether MigrationClosure may be an additional durable Registry model
questions: Is the durable MigrationClosure an allowed additional Registry model despite State 0's exhaustive storage boundary, or must migration closure be represented using an already permitted fact such as the audit log or configuration?

topics.topic: Whether whole-Project deletion also deletes its ArtifactPointers
questions: When a Project is deleted whole, are its ArtifactPointer records also deleted?

topics.topic: Which ArtifactPointers are included in the agent projection
questions: Which ArtifactPointer records does reading the agent projection return?

topics.topic: Who performs AgentSession access and pending-request mutations
questions: Is the pending request and its access-version change a mutation of AgentSession performed by Kernel for the agent, or is every AgentSession access mutation performed by the owner alone?
